recipe.title: Poulet au citron, tomates et piment braisé
recipe.description: Mijoté de cuisses de poulet parfumé au citron, tomates fraîches et piment, relevé d'ail et de concentré de tomate. Un plat réconfortant aux accents ouest‑africains, servi avec du riz.

Coupe les tomates en quartiers.
Râpe le zeste du citron puis presse son jus.

Retire le poulet et réserve‑le.

Assaisonne avec 1 pincée de sel et de poivre.

Couvre et laisse cuire à feu doux 12 minutes, jusqu'à absorption complète de l'eau et grains tendres.

recipe.title: Soy‑Ginger Chicken Stir‑Fry with Broccoli over Rice
recipe.description: Quick stir‑fried chicken thighs with ginger, garlic and soy sauce, tossed with broccoli and served over fluffy rice.
instructions: Rinse the 200 g of rice under cold water, then add to a pot with 400 ml water. Bring to a boil over medium heat, cover and simmer 12 minutes, until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit covered for 3 minutes; fluff with a fork.
While the rice cooks, cut the chicken thighs into bite‑size strips.
Trim the broccoli into small florets; rinse and set aside.
Peel and finely mince the 2 cloves of garlic and the 1 tbsp of grated ginger.

Heat 2 tbsp of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium‑high heat. Add the chicken strips and stir‑fry 5 minutes, until the surface is golden and the internal temperature reaches 74 °C (no pinkness).
Add the minced garlic and ginger; stir‑fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the broccoli florets, toss and cook 3 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Pour in 3 tbsp soy sauce, stir to coat, and season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Cook 1 minute more, letting the sauce thicken slightly.
Serve the chicken‑broccoli stir‑fry over the cooked rice, sprinkled with 2 tbsp sliced spring onions.
tips: Cut the chicken into uniform pieces for even cooking.
If you like a little heat, add a pinch of red pepper flakes with the garlic.
Use a lid to steam the broccoli for 2 minutes if you prefer it softer.

recipe.description: Oven‑baked chicken thighs glazed with garlic‑ginger sauce, paired with simply steamed broccoli and a quick fried‑egg rice bowl.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Pat the chicken thighs dry, then place them on a baking tray lined with foil.

Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium heat, add a little oil, and crack the 2 eggs. Fry 2 minutes for sunny‑side‑up, until whites are set and yolks still runny.
Trim the broccoli into florets, place in a steamer basket over simmering water, cover and steam 5 minutes, until tender‑crisp.

tips: For extra caramelisation, broil the chicken for the last 2 minutes.
If you prefer the egg fully cooked, flip it after 1 minute and cook another minute.
Reserve any leftover glaze to drizzle over the broccoli.

recipe.title: Chicken & Broccoli Egg‑Drop Soup
recipe.description: Light, comforting broth flavored with ginger and soy, loaded with shredded chicken, broccoli and silky egg ribbons – perfect for a quick dinner.
instructions: Trim the broccoli into very small florets (about 1‑cm pieces).

Turn the heat to low; slowly pour the beaten eggs into the soup in a thin stream while gently stirring with a fork, creating silky ribbons. Cook 1 minute more, until the egg is set.
Ladle the soup into bowls and garnish each with 1 tbsp sliced spring onions.

recipe.title: Tacos de frijol negro y aguacate
recipe.description: Tacos rápidos y llenos de sabor con frijoles negros, aguacate fresco, queso y un toque de lima.
instructions: Calienta 1 cda de aceite vegetal en una sartén a fuego medio.
Añade la cebolla morada picada y sofríe 3 minutos, hasta que esté translúcida.

Arma los tacos colocando una porción de frijoles en cada tortilla, luego agrega cubos de aguacate, queso fresco desmenuzado y un chorrito de jugo de lima restante.
Sirve inmediatamente.

recipe.title: Arroz con maíz, huevo frito y lima
recipe.description: Arroz suelto mezclado con maíz dulce, tomate y huevo frito, ideal para un almuerzo nutritivo y rápido.
instructions: Enjuaga el arroz bajo agua corriente hasta que el agua salga clara.
En una olla mediana, calienta 1 cda de aceite a fuego medio y añade el arroz. Sofríe 2 minutos, sin que se dore.
Agrega 400 ml de agua, una pizca de sal y lleva a ebullición. Reduce el fuego a bajo, tapa y cocina 12 minutos, hasta que el agua se absorba y el arroz esté tierno.
Mientras se cocina el arroz, calienta 1 cda de aceite en una sartén a fuego medio.
Añade la cebolla morada picada y sofríe 3 minutos, hasta que esté dorada.
Incorpora los tomates picados y cocina 2 minutos más.
Escurre el maíz de la lata y añádelo a la sartén; cocina 2 minutos, mezclando con la cebolla y el tomate.
Cuando el arroz esté listo, incorpora la mezcla de maíz, tomate y cebolla al arroz y revuelve bien; ajusta con sal y pimienta.
En la misma sartén, agrega un chorrito de aceite y fríe los 2 huevos a fuego medio, 3 minutos por lado, hasta que la clara esté firme y la yema ligeramente cuajada.
Sirve el arroz con maíz en platos, coloca un huevo frito encima de cada porción y exprime el jugo de la lima sobre todo.
tips: Puedes añadir un poco de cilantro picado al final para más frescura.
Si prefieres el huevo revuelto, hazlo en la misma sartén antes de mezclar con el arroz.

recipe.title: Riz sauté au poulet rôti, courgettes et œuf
recipe.description: Un plat rapide où le riz cuit et le poulet rôti se transforment en un sauté coloré, relevé d'œuf poché et d'emmental fondant.
instructions: Émince l'oignon en fines lamelles.
Coupe les courgettes en julienne (bâtonnets fins).
Dans une poêle ou un wok, fais chauffer 1 c. à soupe d'huile d'olive à feu moyen.
Ajoute l'oignon et fais-le dorer 3 minutes, jusqu'à ce qu'il devienne translucide.
Incorpore les courgettes, fais sauter 4 minutes, jusqu'à ce qu'elles soient légèrement tendres mais encore croquantes.

Réchauffe le riz cuit et le poulet rôti émietté dans la poêle : ajoute les 2 portions de riz et le poulet, mélange et fais chauffer 3 minutes, jusqu'à ce que le riz soit fumant à cœur et le poulet bien chaud.
Fais sauter le tout 2 minutes supplémentaires, en remuant, pour obtenir une légère coloration du riz.
Assaisonne avec 1 pincée de sel et 1 pincée de poivre.

Pendant ce temps, porte une petite casserole d'eau à frémissement, crée un tourbillon et dépose délicatement les 2 œufs pour les pocher 3 minutes, jusqu'à ce que le blanc soit ferme et le jaune encore coulant.
Retire les œufs avec une écumoire, égoutte-les légèrement et dispose-les sur le riz sauté.
Parseme le dessus de 50 g d'emmental râpé, laisse fondre quelques secondes avant de servir.
tips: Utilise une poêle bien chaude pour obtenir des grains de riz légèrement croustillants.
Si tu aimes le piquant, ajoute une pointe de piment d'Espelette à l'étape d'assaisonnement.

recipe.title: Mediterranean Quinoa Stuffed Aubergine Boats
recipe.description: Tender aubergine halves baked with a savory quinoa, chickpea, tomato and spinach filling, finished with a bright lemon‑tahini drizzle.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Slice each aubergine lengthwise and scoop out a shallow well, leaving about 1 cm of flesh attached to the skin.
Brush the aubergine halves with 1 tbsp olive oil, season with salt and pepper, and place cut‑side up on a baking tray.
Bake for 15 minutes on medium heat, until the flesh is softened but still holds shape.
Rinse the quinoa, then add 150 g quinoa and 300 ml water to a saucepan; bring to a boil, reduce to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook 12 minutes until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
While quinoa cooks, heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the chopped tomatoes (3 pieces) and cook 5 minutes, stirring, until they start to break down.
Stir in the spinach (150 g) and cook 2 minutes until wilted.
Add the chickpeas (200 g, canned – drained and rinsed) and the cooked quinoa to the skillet; mix well and season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Cook 3 minutes to combine flavors.
Fill each aubergine half with the quinoa‑chickpea mixture, smoothing the top.
Return the stuffed aubergines to the oven and bake 10 minutes, until the tops are golden.
Meanwhile, whisk together the tahini (2 tbsp), juice of the lemon, and 2 tbsp water until smooth and drizzle‑y.
Drizzle the lemon‑tahini sauce over the baked aubergine boats and serve warm.
tips: If the quinoa seems dry, add a splash more water while mixing with the vegetables.
For extra crunch, sprinkle toasted pine nuts on top just before serving.

recipe.title: One‑Pot Mediterranean Chickpea & Spinach Stew
recipe.description: A hearty, quick stew where chickpeas, tomatoes and spinach mingle in a fragrant lemon‑tahini broth, perfect for a light dinner.
instructions: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the minced garlic (2 cloves) and sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the cumin powder and cook 30 seconds.
Dice the tomatoes (4 pieces) and add them to the pot; cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they soften.
Add the chickpeas (400 g, canned – drained and rinsed), water (400 ml), and a pinch of salt and pepper. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a low simmer.
Simmer for 15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld; the broth should thicken slightly.
Fold in the spinach (200 g) and cook 2 minutes, just until wilted.
In a small bowl, whisk together the tahini (3 tbsp), juice of the lemon, and 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Stir the lemon‑tahini sauce into the stew; heat another 2 minutes, watching for the sauce to emulsify and coat the vegetables.
Taste and adjust seasoning with extra salt or pepper if needed, then serve hot.
tips: For a richer broth, replace part of the water with low‑salt vegetable stock.
Garnish with a sprinkle of chopped fresh parsley or a drizzle of extra tahini.

recipe.title: Quick Lemon‑Tahini Quinoa Salad with Roasted Aubergine and Spinach
recipe.description: A light, refreshing salad combining fluffy quinoa, smoky roasted aubergine, fresh spinach and a zesty lemon‑tahini dressing – ready in under an hour.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Dice the aubergine (1 piece) into 2 cm cubes, toss with 2 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt and pepper, and spread on a baking sheet.
Roast the aubergine cubes for 20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.

Rinse the quinoa, then place 200 g quinoa with 400 ml water in a saucepan; bring to a boil, cover, and simmer 12 minutes until water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let sit covered 5 minutes, then fluff.
While quinoa cooks, chop the tomatoes (2 pieces) into bite‑size pieces.
In a large bowl combine the cooked quinoa, roasted aubergine, fresh spinach (150 g), and chopped tomatoes.
Prepare the dressing: whisk together tahini (3 tbsp), juice of the lemon, 2 tbsp water, and 1 tbsp olive oil until smooth; season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
Serve the salad at room temperature or slightly chilled.
tips: For extra protein, add a handful of cooked chickpeas (use leftover from pantry if desired).
If you prefer a thinner dressing, add an additional tablespoon of water.

recipe.description: Des moitiés de courgettes cuites au four jusqu'à ce qu'elles soient dorées, avec un œuf cuit au centre pour un dîner léger et rassasiant.

recipe.title: Salmón a la plancha con arroz de limón y judías verdes salteadas
recipe.description: Salmón dorado a la plancha servido sobre arroz aromatizado con limón y acompañado de judías verdes salteadas al ajo.
instructions: Enjuaga el arroz bajo agua fría y colócalo en una olla con 400 ml de agua y una pizca de sal; lleva a ebullición, reduce a fuego medio‑bajo y cocina 15 minutos, hasta que el agua se absorba y el arroz esté tierno al pinchar con un tenedor.
Mientras se cuece el arroz, corta las judías verdes en trozos de 4 cm.
Calienta 1 cda de aceite de oliva en una sartén a fuego medio y saltea el ajo picado 1 minuto, hasta que esté fragante.
Añade las judías verdes, sazona con sal y pimienta, y saltea 6‑8 minutos, removiendo ocasionalmente, hasta que estén tiernas pero crujientes.
Ralla la cáscara del limón y exprime su jugo; mezcla ambos al arroz ya cocido y remueve 1 minuto a fuego bajo para que se impregne.
Seca los filetes de salmón con papel de cocina y sazona con sal y pimienta.

Calienta 2 cda de aceite de oliva en una sartén antiadherente a fuego medio‑alto; coloca los filetes con la piel hacia abajo (si la tienen) y cocina 4‑5 minutos, hasta que se doren. Voltea y cocina 3‑4 minutos más, hasta que la temperatura interna alcance 63 °C y la carne sea opaca y se despegue en láminas.
Sirve el salmón sobre una cama de arroz de limón y acompaña con las judías verdes salteadas.
tips: No levantes la tapa del arroz mientras se cocina; el vapor es clave para una textura suelta.
Para un toque extra, espolvorea perejil fresco picado al final.

recipe.title: Sopa ligera de patata y limón con trozos de salmón
recipe.description: Una sopa cremosa sin lácteos, hecha con patata, caldo vegetal y limón, finalizada con trozos de salmón cocido al instante.
instructions: Pela las patatas y córtalas en cubos de 1 cm.
En una olla mediana, calienta 1 cda de aceite a fuego medio y añade las patatas; sofríe 3 minutos, hasta que empiecen a dorarse ligeramente.
Agrega el caldo vegetal y lleva a ebullición; reduce a fuego medio‑bajo y cocina 10 minutos, hasta que las patatas estén tiernas.
Añade el arroz y cocina 12 minutos más, hasta que esté blando y la sopa haya espesado ligeramente.
Mientras la sopa hierve, corta el salmón en cubos de 2 cm.
Cuando la sopa esté lista, reduce el fuego a bajo, incorpora el jugo y la ralladura de medio limón, y ajusta de sal y pimienta.
Añade los cubos de salmón a la sopa caliente; cocina 3‑4 minutos, removiendo suavemente, hasta que el salmón alcance 63 °C (la carne se volverá opaca y se deshará en trozos).
Sirve la sopa en cuencos, decorando con una rodaja fina de limón.
tips: Si la sopa queda muy espesa, añade un poco más de caldo o agua caliente.
Para mayor frescura, agrega unas hojas de cilantro picado justo antes de servir.

recipe.title: Herb‑Roasted Pork Tenderloin with Dijon‑Cream Sauce and Green Beans
recipe.description: A light dinner featuring juicy pork tenderloin glazed with Dijon mustard, finished in a creamy sauce, served alongside crisp green beans.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Pat the pork tenderloin dry, then rub it with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 pinch salt, 1 pinch pepper, and the thyme sprigs.
Mix 2 tbsp Dijon mustard with the pork and place the tenderloin on a baking sheet.
Roast the pork for 20‑25 minutes, until the internal temperature reaches 63°C and the juices run clear; let rest 5 minutes.
While the pork roasts, trim the green beans and toss them with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 pinch salt, and 1 pinch pepper.
Spread the beans on a separate baking tray and add the sliced shallots; roast together with the pork for the last 12 minutes, until beans are tender‑crisp and shallots are caramelised.
In a small saucepan, combine the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and the shallot slices (removed from the tray) over medium heat; sauté 2 minutes until soft.
Add the cream, stir, and simmer 5 minutes on medium heat, until the sauce thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon.
Slice the rested pork tenderloin into 1‑cm medallions, drizzle with the Dijon‑cream sauce, and serve with the roasted green beans.
tips: If you prefer a richer sauce, add a splash of white wine before the cream and reduce.
Use the same pan to deglaze the pork drippings for extra flavour.

recipe.title: Leek & Shallot Gruyère Gratin
recipe.description: A comforting, low‑carb gratin where sweet leeks and aromatic shallots are baked under a golden Gruyère crust.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Trim the root ends and dark green tops of the leeks; slice them lengthwise, rinse well, and cut into 1‑cm thick half‑moons.
Peel the shallots and thinly slice them.
In a large skillet, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat; add the leeks and shallots, season with 1 pinch salt and 1 pinch pepper, and sauté 8 minutes until softened but not browned.
Stir in 100 ml cream, a pinch of nutmeg, and continue cooking 2 minutes until the mixture thickens slightly.
Transfer the leek‑shallot mixture to a greased baking dish, spreading evenly.
Grate the Gruyère and sprinkle the entire surface with the cheese.
Bake for 20‑25 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and turns a deep golden brown.
Remove from oven, let rest 5 minutes, then serve warm.
tips: For extra depth, add a splash of dry white wine to the skillet before the cream.
A light drizzle of extra‑virgin olive oil after baking adds a nice sheen.

recipe.title: Creamy Leek, Green‑Bean & Pork Consommé Soup
recipe.description: A clear yet velvety soup that combines the remaining pork tenderloin, leeks, and green beans, finished with a touch of cream for richness.
instructions: Trim the pork tenderloin and cut 200 g into thin strips; season with 1 pinch salt and 1 pinch pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat; add the pork strips and sear 4 minutes, turning until lightly browned. Remove and set aside.
Thinly slice the leeks (white and light green parts only) and finely dice the shallot.
In the same pot, add the shallot and leeks; sauté 5 minutes over medium heat until softened.
Add the green beans, cut into 2‑cm pieces, and pour in 1 l of stock.
Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a low simmer; cook 15 minutes until the beans are tender.
Return the pork strips to the pot and continue simmering 5 minutes, ensuring the pork reaches an internal temperature of 63°C.
Stir in 80 ml cream, heat 2 minutes without boiling, and adjust seasoning with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with chopped fresh parsley, and serve immediately.
tips: If you have leftover pork from the first recipe, use it here to reduce waste.
For a clearer broth, strain the soup before adding cream and then return the solids to the pot.
